# StreamBus ground truths (v2, 0.2.0)

- Registration: `services.AddStreamBus((context, cfg) => ...)` for the
  default bus, `services.AddStreamBus<TBus>((context, cfg) => ...)` per
  extra bus. Configuration is explicit and fluent only: there is no
  `IConfiguration` overload, no `appsettings.json` binding, and no automatic
  discovery. Every option is a configurator method call and is validated
  once at registration.
- `cfg.Host(host, vhost, h => h.Credentials(user, password))` exactly
  once per bus. Empty credentials are rejected; `guest`/`guest` is
  accepted for a local broker, and remote deployments should use a
  dedicated non-`guest` user. Defaults: StreamPort 5552, AmqpPort 5672
  (queue dead letters and error-queue requeues; otherwise no AMQP
  connection), Heartbeat 60s, MonitorInterval 5s (must be >0 and <=60s),
  pools 1/1.
- Typed publish: `cfg.Publish<T>(stream)` for plain streams,
  `cfg.PublishSuper<T>(stream, s => s.Partitions(n))` for super streams.
  `bus.PublishAsync(msg)` / `bus.PublishAsync(stream, msg)` are plain;
  `bus.PublishSuperAsync(msg, key)` /
  `bus.PublishSuperAsync(stream, msg, key)` are super with a required
  routing key. Wrong method for the registration is a config error.
  Same message type on two streams of one bus is an ambiguity error.
  Explicit-stream targets on undeclared streams raise
  `StreamBusStreamNotFoundException` and never auto-create. Raw bytes go
  through `bus.PublishRawAsync`, which does not run publish filters.
- Consumer identity: `cfg.ReceiveEndpoint(stream, e =>
  e.Consumer<TConsumer>("group"))`. The group is required, verbatim,
  max 255 bytes, exactly one `Consumer` call per endpoint. Same group
  scales out via a shared cursor; different groups are independent
  cursors. Raw `ConsumeAsync` also requires `Reference`. The library
  never derives group names.
- Cross-process caveat: same reference, `SingleActiveConsumer = false`,
  two processes: both receive deliveries (at-least-once doubles, never
  skips). Stores interleave; a stale process may regress the broker-side
  offset - never run two writers on one reference outside SAC.
- Startup topology derives from endpoint registrations, publish
  registrations, and stream dead-letter destinations. Endpoints adopt
  broker reality (matching kind consumed read-only, mismatch conflicts,
  missing declarable streams are declared, otherwise config error).
  Publish/endpoint kinds must agree with the merged declarations.
  Runtime/operator declarations use
  `bus.Topology.EnsureStreamAsync` / `EnsureSuperStreamAsync`.
  Single-partition reads are plain consumes of `{super}-{N}` with no
  declaration.
- Retry: `cfg.UseMessageRetry(...)` global default, per-endpoint
  override, `UseRetry` escape hatches. Schedules: Immediate, Interval,
  Intervals, Exponential, None. Unbounded default retries forever
  (`Strict`); `Strict` plus any hand-off destination or callback is a
  configuration error.
- Exhaustion: bounded + `DeadLetterToStream` / `DeadLetterToQueue` hands
  off; bounded + `OnExhausted` callback owns the outcome (return advances,
  throw recycles; declared destinations shadowed with a warning); bounded
  + neither hands off to the derived classic queue `{stream}_error`;
  unbounded + either is a config error.
- Error destinations: `DeadLetterToStream(name, spec?)` uses a declared
  error stream with envelope semantics, advance-once, and
  `ReplayErrorStreamAsync`; `DeadLetterToQueue(name, DeadLetterQueueType)`
  uses a durable classic or quorum AMQP queue with `streambus.error.*`
  headers and `RequeueErrorsAsync`. Queue destinations are declared by
  the AMQP transport, never by topology.
- Hand-off timeouts: stream hand-offs use
  `e.ErrorHandoffTimeout(timeout)` (default 10s, values below 1s are
  raised to 1s); queue hand-offs use
  `DeadLetterToQueue(name, type, q => q.ConfirmTimeout(timeout))`
  (default 10s). A lost confirmation surfaces as a timeout/transient
  failure with an unknown outcome; the envelope stays replayable.
- Startup blocking is service-level:
  `services.AddStreamBusHosting(h =>
  h.BlockStartupUntilReady(timeout?))`, at most once; default is
  non-blocking. Blocking startup waits for connections, topology, and
  typed consumer attaches by default; `h.BlockUntilConsumersAttached(false)`
  opts out of the consumer wait. A consumer that cannot attach raises
  `StreamBusStartupBlockedException`; a budget expiry raises
  `StreamBusTimeoutException`.
- Health: the `streambus` check reports connection state under
  `{vhost}|{busType}` and per-registration rows under
  `{vhost}|{registration}` (`consumer:<state>` / `declare:<state>`,
  including reason and since). No buses registered is degraded. Healthy
  means every registration attached and every connection ready; degraded
  means starting/retrying or some consumers retrying; unhealthy means a
  fatal connection, an exhausted declaration, or all typed consumers
  failed.
- Pipelines: `UsePublishFilter` and `UseConsumeFilter` are additive and
  repeatable, with no cap; execution is exactly registration order and
  the first registered filter is outermost (first in, last out). Consume
  filters registered on the bus run before endpoint filters. Duplicate
  filter types within one scope are configuration errors. Publish filters
  must call `next` exactly once and cannot short-circuit; consume filters
  may skip only when `CanSkip` is true; typed endpoints must also call
  `AllowPipelineSkip()`, raw endpoints skip without opt-in, and
  effectively-once pipelines reject skippable filters at attach.
- Effectively-once (`ConsumeEffectivelyOnceAsync`) stores no source
  offsets and publishes results with `publishing-id = source offset`.
  Resume is recomputed from the target; one pipeline per (source, target)
  pair.
- Observability: meter `StreamBus` (`streambus_partition_lag/_inflight/_retry_blocked`,
  `streambus_connection_state`, `streambus_offset_store_rejected_total`,
  `streambus_offset_regressed_total`, `streambus_offset_fallback_total`,
  `streambus_pipeline_duration` histogram).
- Exceptions: every StreamBus exception derives from
  `StreamBusException`. Configuration and topology-conflict failures are
  permanent; `StreamBusNotReadyException` is transient;
  `StreamBusStreamNotFoundException` is permanent once the bus is ready
  (a blocking startup attach may retry it while streams are still being
  created); timeouts have an unknown outcome and may be retried when the
  operation is safe;
  `StreamBusPublishTransientException` is retryable while
  `StreamBusPublishException` is not; `StreamBusFatalException` requires
  reconnection/operator action.
